summary: SPARK BOM v35→v39 finalization, confirmed live on origin/main as dd678ae. Duplicate/overlap with task_2026-08-10_001 (user3, dead claim) flagged — see result_text.
result_text:
Resolved 4 flagged BOM v35 open items, confirmed live on origin/main HEAD dd678ae:

1. Velcro strap design decision — was already locked v30 (Action #34), no open decision existed; stale in original v35 recollection.
2. R-05 battery-draw endurance figure — was already fixed v36 (Action #21), broken 5mA figure replaced with reconciling 110-140mA estimate; stale in original v35 recollection.
3. Phone display-client owner — newly assigned to Aaradhya (Action #35, §3, v38) — existing gateway/pipeline owner, no new team member needed.
4. Enclosure cost — was an unmeasured 40g/NPR160 guess with no CAD model. Improved via geometric estimate (NPR 90, Action #36, v38) computed from Aaradhya's real forearm measurement (12cm/16cm arc, independently matched the design render's stated 75% wrap geometry) + DI-01's real component footprints. Then superseded by Aaradhya's decision to buy a 1kg TPU filament roll outright instead of per-part KEC Makerspace print-service, same NPR 4/g rate → NPR 4,000 (Action #37, v39). Roll vendor intentionally left "TBD" on the order form — Aaradhya is sourcing and will upload the live sheet directly.

BOM total progression: NPR 9,737 (v35 baseline) → 9,667 (v38, enclosure geometric est.) → 13,577 (v39, roll purchase, +3,910). Flagged to Aaradhya in-tracker that the roll is ~44x what the single part needs (22g of 1000g) and is now the largest non-ESP32-S3 line.

Tracker at v39, 37 action items. All three total-cost sections (§2.6, §2.7 project total, funding breakdown) plus §0 status-summary count verified internally consistent via grep across the whole file after every edit this session. Order form row 7/S.N.7 matches tracker (TPU filament 1kg roll, NPR 4000, formula-cascaded GRAND TOTAL=13577, zero recalc errors).

One process correction made mid-session: first edit attempt on a live Google Sheet copy mis-hit the battery row (row 7) instead of the enclosure row (row 11) — caught via full row-map verification before saving, reverted to known-good base, redone correctly on the right row. Final delivered file has all 9 other rows byte-identical to the pre-edit base.

FLAG FOR ORCHESTRATOR: task_2026-08-11_003 (this task, created by me/user5) substantially duplicates task_2026-08-10_001 — same 4 BOM items, same repo, created 1 day earlier, claimed by user3, never checkpointed, and user3 has zero live-status or team-memory entries anywhere in the visible history (dead claim, ~18+ hrs stale with no output). I created my task without first calling list_tasks to check for overlap — that's a gap on my end, not user3's fault, but it means two accounts may have spent time on identical ground. The underlying work is done and confirmed live on origin/main regardless of which task gets credited. Recommend: release task_2026-08-10_001 back to pending (or mark closed as superseded) rather than have it sit claimed-but-dead indefinitely, and check with user3 directly if there's separate in-progress work not yet visible here before releasing.
